raw_response:
I've been farming this land for over fifty years. My family depends on what I grow, and at my age, I can't take big risks or try things I don't know. My back isn't what it was — I still do most of the work myself but my son helps during harvest.

Here in Quzhou, we all grow wheat in the winter and corn in the summer. That's what the land here is suited for, that's what the market buys, and that's what I know how to grow. I have about 8 mu of cropland. I'll plant all of it in this rotation — nothing fancy.

For wheat, I'll use the improved variety the seed shop in town has been selling — it's what my neighbors use and the yields are decent. Same for corn, I'll get a hybrid from the township supply co-op. I've started using hybrid corn the last several years because the ears are bigger.

Water is always the worry. The well here is getting deeper every year. I'll water the wheat three times — once when I sow it, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. For corn, rain usually helps in summer, but I'll water twice to be safe.

I'll put fertilizer down by hand the way I always have — base fertilizer before planting, then a top dressing. I don't do soil tests. I go by what my father taught me and what has worked.

For tillage, I rent a rotary tiller for wheat. For corn, I sow directly into the wheat stubble now — saves diesel and the soil holds moisture better.

I'll spray herbicide once on the wheat in winter, and once for insects before heading. For corn, one spray should be enough.
